newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on profit taking, debate.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on profit taking, debate.

text.p: Thai stocks fell on Wednesday for the second day in a row as trade remained thin while investors watched a censure debate against the prime minister, brokers said.

The SET index moved in negative territory throughout the day to end down 12.32 points at 1,038.03. Total turnover was a slim 2.7 billion baht. Decliners led gainers 226 to 76 with 90 issues unchanged. The SET-50 index slipped 1.01 points to 79.60.
"Retailers sold and took profits as they waited for the outcome of the debate," said Suleeyaporn Tasanasrit of UBS (East Asia) Securities.
A no-confidence debate against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa began on Wednesday and is due to last three days.
The main activitiy was some light profit taking in the market following recent rises on the bourse, brokers said.
"Investors were reluctant to enter the market as they waited for the outcome of the debate," Suleeyaporn said.
Brokers said the market was sluggish because a private fund which was set up to assist the bourse was not active on Wednesday.
Part of the 15.7 billion baht fund, contributed by commercial banks and brokerages, has been invested in the market since September 6.
Large capitalised Bangkok Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 220 baht. Alphatec Electronics retreated 28 to 262 and Sun Wood Industries slipped 1.75 to 17.75.

"The index is expected to fall tomorrow because investors are expected to stay on the sidelines awaiting the outcome of the no-confidence debate," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.
